name: Consent Collector JP
author: YPSupport

sections.description:
Consent Collector JP is a Cookie consent management (CMP) plugin for Japanese website operators, built to comply with the “External Transmission Rules” of Japan’s Telecommunications Business Act (effective June 2023) and the amended Act on the Protection of Personal Information.

Under the External Transmission Rules, when a website sends visitor information to external services via Cookies or similar technologies, the site must notify or publicly disclose what is sent, to whom, and for what purpose. This plugin centers on automatically generating that disclosure page, alongside a consent banner and server-side consent logging.

This plugin does not provide legal advice. The accuracy and legal compliance of the generated content is the responsibility of the site operator.

Key Features

  • Automatically generates an external transmission disclosure page: Built-in templates for the 6 most common services — Google Analytics (GA4), Google Tag Manager, Google AdSense, Meta Pixel, YouTube embeds, and X (Twitter) embeds. Any other service can also be registered manually, so full legal compliance is possible with the free version alone.
  • First-run setup wizard: After activation, the wizard walks you through selecting the services you use from the built-in templates, configuring the banner, and registering scripts.
  • No dark patterns: Implied consent (e.g. “scrolling counts as consent”) and cookie walls are not implemented, not even as an option. The “Accept All” and “Essential Only” buttons always have equal visual weight.
  • Zero external requests, lightweight: The banner never loads external fonts or CDN resources. Additional HTTP requests are kept to a minimum.
  • No external connections for its core functionality: The consent banner, tag blocking, and external transmission disclosure page all run entirely on your own server; no visitor data is ever sent to this plugin’s developer or to any third party as part of that functionality. (The bundled Freemius licensing library contacts Freemius’s servers solely for license validation and update checks, as is standard for commercially licensed WordPress plugins; this does not involve visitor data. The optional Premium GeoIP feature also downloads a public IP-to-country database file from db-ip.com roughly once a month to enable region-based banner behavior.)
  • Consent logs stored on your own server: No consent records are transferred to servers outside your control. The visitor’s IP address is never stored — not even a hashed or otherwise derived value. Each log row is identified only by a random ID generated in the visitor’s browser. Log retention is the same for every user: logs are kept indefinitely by default, and you can optionally set a retention period (e.g. delete logs older than 30 days) from the settings screen.
  • Fully compatible with page caching: All banner display and consent-state logic run client-side in JavaScript, so the plugin works correctly even on sites using static page caching.
  • Google Consent Mode v2 (basic): Automatically sends the “denied” default and per-category consent/withdrawal signals to gtag() for sites already using Google tags (GA4 / Google Ads), so those tags respect visitor consent out of the box. Does nothing if the site has no gtag() defined.
  • Re-consent when your policy changes: Update the “banner version” setting and every visitor — including those who already consented — will be asked again the next time they visit.
  • Visitors can change or withdraw their consent at any time — withdrawals are logged just like consents, and automatically propagated to Google Consent Mode v2.

Disclaimer

This plugin is a tool to help support compliance with Japan’s Telecommunications Business Act and Act on the Protection of Personal Information. It does not provide legal advice. Please consult a qualified professional (attorney, gyoseishoshi, etc.) as needed to confirm actual legal compliance.

References

  • Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications: External Transmission Rules (Japanese)
  • Related FAQ (Japanese)
sections.installation:
1. Upload and activate the plugin.
  2. The first-run setup wizard will appear automatically. Follow the on-screen steps to select the services you use, and configure the banner.
  3. You can change any setting at any time from the “Consent Collector JP” menu.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin guarantee full legal compliance?

No. This plugin is a tool to help support compliance, not a substitute for legal advice. Whether the generated disclosures and your actual site operation meet applicable legal requirements is the responsibility of the site operator.

What are Japan’s “External Transmission Rules”?

They are rules under Japan’s Telecommunications Business Act (effective June 2023) that require operators to notify or publicly disclose the content, destination, and purpose of visitor information sent to external providers via Cookies or similar technologies. See the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications’ explanatory pages for details.

Does this work with page caching plugins?

Yes. Banner display and consent-state logic run entirely in the visitor’s browser (JavaScript); the server never outputs different HTML per visitor. The plugin is designed to work alongside common page-caching setups.

Is there a difference in legal compliance capability between the free and Premium versions?

No. The free version alone, combined with templates and manual registration, can achieve full legal compliance. The Premium version adds convenience, ongoing monitoring, and multilingual/international features — it does not gate compliance itself behind a paywall.

What if another plugin or my theme already outputs a tag like Google Analytics?

Tags such as Google Analytics (GA4) must be registered through this plugin’s “Categories & Tags” tab to be covered by its pre-consent blocking and Google Consent Mode integration. A tag output directly by another plugin or by your theme is outside this plugin’s control — it will run regardless of visitor consent, and registering the same tag here as well would only cause it to load twice. If another plugin or your theme is already outputting such a tag, disable that output first, then register the tag through this plugin’s “Categories & Tags” tab instead.

Can visitors withdraw their consent?

Yes. A re-consent link — the [ypcm_reconsent] shortcode or a footer link — lets visitors change or withdraw consent at any time. After withdrawal, the affected tags will no longer be loaded on subsequent page views, and withdrawals are recorded with the same detail as consents.
sections.changelog:
1.0.4

  • Security: Improved how the visitor’s IP address is determined when a trusted proxy is configured. The plugin now reads the last value of the X-Forwarded-For header instead of the first, because the first value can be set freely by the client. This only affects sites that have configured trusted proxies for the Pro geolocation feature.
  • Security: Trusted proxy entries are now validated when saved. A malformed CIDR entry (for example 203.0.113.10/foo) was previously treated as /0, which matches every address. Invalid lines are now removed on save and a notice is shown so the mistake is visible.

1.0.3

  • Fix: Banner styles are no longer overridden by theme CSS. Some themes styled the banner buttons and links with their own colors; the plugin’s own styles now take precedence. If you customize the banner with your own CSS, use selectors that include .ypcm-banner (e.g. .ypcm-banner .ypcm-btn).
  • Fix: Updated reference and opt-out links for several bundled service templates. Some destinations had moved, and two opt-out links (Facebook, Instagram) led to a login screen — they now point to a page you can read without signing in. Existing entries are not changed automatically; you can review and apply the updates from the destinations screen in a future release.
  • New: Added an option to display the “Essential Only” button with the same visual weight as “Accept All” (Settings > Banner tab). Off by default.
  • New (Premium): Visitors can now view the list of external data recipients (service name, data sent, purpose, consent category) directly inside the consent banner, without leaving the page (Settings > Banner tab, off by default). This shows the same destination data as the generated External Transmission Policy page; the page’s introductory text, cookie explanation, and disclaimer are not duplicated here. On multilingual banners, this detail view is Japanese-only even when the rest of the banner is translated.
  • Security: The Premium in-banner detail endpoint no longer responds when its setting is turned off. Also hardened the same endpoint against corrupted destination data, so a damaged setting no longer causes a server error.

1.0.2

  • Fix: Scripts registered with both inline code and an external script URL are now output as two separate tags, so the inline code runs correctly after consent. Previously the inline part never executed because browsers ignore the body of a script tag that has a src attribute. This issue affected such registrations (including the standard GA4 snippet) since 1.0.0. Workaround registrations (code and URL as two separate tags) continue to work and need no change.
  • New: Generated external-transmission policy pages now include a re-consent link (“Cookie・同意設定を変更する”) so visitors can always change or withdraw consent. Existing pages gain the link on next regeneration.
  • New: Documented the consent withdrawal feature (readme, admin help tab). Withdrawal link display text unified.
  • Internal: Added template snapshot storage (groundwork for template-update notifications in a future release).

1.0.1

  • Security: If your site sits behind a reverse proxy or CDN, detecting the visitor’s real IP address (used for the consent rate limit and Premium’s GeoIP feature) now requires you to specify which proxies to trust, instead of a simple on/off switch. This closes a way a visitor could fake their IP address to get around the rate limit. If you previously had this turned on, please revisit the GeoIP settings tab to re-enter your trusted proxies — you’ll see a notice there guiding you through it.
  • Security: The Premium site scanner’s background page check now verifies SSL certificates by default.
  • Fix: Made the Premium GeoIP database update more robust, so an interrupted update can no longer leave the database in a broken state.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
